# Synthetic package fixtures

All files contain synthetic test data, not game content.

- `ps3-list-explicit.pkg`: retail PS3 package with explicit parent directories.
- `ps3-list-implied.pkg`: debug PS3 package with inferred parent directories.
  Both represent the tree in `docs/explore-selection.md`.
- `ps4-nested.pkg`: fake PS4 package with encrypted outer PFS, mixed raw/zlib
  PFSC blocks, inner application PFS, an empty directory, a zero-byte file and
  container metadata mapped to `sce_sys/param.sfo`.
- `ps4-selection.pkg`: the Explore selection contract tree plus container metadata
  under `sce_sys/param.sfo`, using the same encrypted/compressed PS4 layout.

Regenerate from the existing format test builders:

```sh
cargo test -p ps3-pkg write_listing_fixtures -- --ignored
cargo test -p ps4-pkg write_listing_fixture -- --ignored
cargo test -p ps4-pkg write_selection_fixture -- --ignored
```

PS4 RSA wrapping uses random padding, so regenerated bytes differ while the
decoded listing stays the same.

## Explore graphical smoke test

With a graphical session, run the synthetic PS3/PS4 browsing and extraction
checks, including the destination picker:

```sh
test_data="$(mktemp -d)"
XDG_DATA_HOME="$test_data" \
GDK_DEBUG=no-portals GSK_RENDERER=cairo G_DEBUG=fatal-criticals \
cargo test -p pkg-gtk tests::explore_tree_selection_and_package_changes -- --ignored --exact
```

The isolated data directory keeps GTK recent-file history out of your normal
profile; remove `$test_data` after testing. `GDK_DEBUG=no-portals` selects GTK's in-process
chooser so the test can drive it. Native portal pickers need a separate manual
check. The PS4 fixture's placeholder SFO cannot pass metadata inspection, so this
test assigns its source directly before using normal listing/extraction workers.
Real-package and large-tree checks are recorded in
[Explore step 7](../../docs/explore-plan.md#7-document-and-validate), including
which GUI paths were not exercised.

## Real-package and manual follow-ups

For each supported local PS3/PS4 package, run the loading smoke test separately
(GTK tests must not share one process across test threads):

```sh
XDG_DATA_HOME="$test_data" \
GDK_DEBUG=no-portals GSK_RENDERER=cairo G_DEBUG=fatal-criticals \
PKG_TOOLS_TEST_PACKAGE=/absolute/path/to/game.pkg \
cargo test -p pkg-gtk tests::blueprint_window_and_package_loading -- --ignored --exact
```

This test checks package loading/metadata and existing UI controls, not real
Explore extraction. For an end-to-end manual check, launch a release build with
the package and open **Explore**. Expand nested folders, scroll, select using
keyboard and Ctrl/Shift-click, then switch pages and confirm selection persists.
Try both extraction buttons with separate empty parent folders; outputs must be
new directories, not merged. Check selected subtrees, overlaps, empty folders,
progress and Cancel. Open another package and confirm listing/selection reset.
Keep source packages unchanged while testing.

To test the desktop's native portal picker, run without `GDK_DEBUG=no-portals`
and confirm that a portal chooser is actually used; the automated Explore test
requires the in-process chooser. Test large-tree browsing separately, recording
entry count, folder width/depth, build profile and renderer. Virtualized widgets
do not eliminate metadata memory or the cost of expanding one very wide folder.
